full_judgment: 23. From the critical analysis of the evidence on record it is abundantly clear to us that the place from where the arms and ammunition were alleged to have been recovered is apparently situated outside the dwelling hut of the appellant and it is an open place where everybody can enter. PW 1, who is the informant, in his cross-examination by the defence, categorically made the distinction between the place of recovery and the house of the defendant which confirms that the place of recovery is an open place accessible to everyone. All other witnesses also corroborated this factual aspect. Fortified with this admitted position which has been confirmed by the evidence on record, presumption of plantation can very well be construed, inasmuch as no evidence  could be found on record proving that the accused appellant himself kept the alleged arms and ammunition in the place from where they were recovered. The law is. very much rigid and settled on this point in so many different cases of our Apex Court.
